## Fonténé's Theorem

::: {#lem-18point1}
Let $R$ be the isogonal conjugate of $Q$, and let $P$ be the Poncelet point of $R$. Then the reflection of $P$ across the $A$-midline is $A_{\perp OQ}$ (so the Steiner line of $P$ with respect to the medial triangle is $OQ$).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
The point $P$ is the center of $(ABCHR)$; let $T$ be the reflection of $H$ across $P$, so that the isogonal conjugate of $T$ is $\infty_{OQ}$.

If $A\infty_{OQ}$ meets $(ABC)$ at $S$, then $AS$ and $AT$ are isogonal lines, so $ST\parallel BC$ (since $S,T\in(ABC)$).

Let $P'$ be the reflection of $P$ across the $A$-midline, let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ across $O$, and let $D$ be the reflection of $H$ across $BC$.

Note that a homothety centered at $H$ with ratio $2$ gives $A_{\perp BC}P\parallel DT$.

Reflecting $A_{\perp BC}P$ across the $A$-midline gives $AP'$, and reflecting $DT$ across the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ gives $A'S$.

Since the midline and perpendicular bisector are perpendicular, we have $AP'\parallel A'S\perp AS\parallel OQ$, so $AP'\perp OQ$.

Since $P$ lies on the nine-point circle, $P'$ lies on the circle with diameter $AO$.

Hence $OQ\perp AP'\perp P'O$, so $O,Q,P'$ are collinear and $P'=A_{\perp OQ}$.
:::

::: {#thm-18point1}
## Fonténé's First Theorem
Let $R$ be the isogonal conjugate of $Q$, and let $P$ be the Poncelet point of $R$. Let $DEF$ be the pedal triangle of $Q$, and set $X=EF\cap M_{AB}M_{AC}$. Then $D,X,P$ are collinear.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Let $P'$ be the reflection of $P$ across $M_{AB}M_{AC}$; by @lem-18point1, $P'=A_{\perp OQ}$.

This is the intersection of $(AQ)$ and $(AO)$, so $P'$ is the Miquel point of $E,M_{AC},M_{AB},F$, giving that $X,P',E,M_{AC}$ are concyclic.

If $D'$ is the reflection of $D$ across the $A$-midline, then $AD'\parallel BC\perp D'Q$, so $A,D',E,F,P',Q$ are concyclic.

Thus
$$
\measuredangle XP'E=\measuredangle XM_{AC}E=\measuredangle D'AE=\measuredangle D'P'E.
$$
Hence $D',P',X$ are collinear, and reflecting across the midline yields that $D,P,X$ are collinear.
:::

::: {#thm-18point2}
## Fonténé's Second Theorem
Let $\ell$ be a line passing through $O$, and let $X$ vary along $\ell$. Then the pedal circle of $X$ passes through a fixed point.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Consider the isogonal conjugate of $\ell$, which is a rectangular hyperbola $\mathcal{H}$ with center $P$.

Let $X'$ be the isogonal conjugate of $X$; by @lem-3point18, the pedal circle of $X$ is the same as the pedal circle of $X'$.

By @lem-14point4, the pedal circle of $X'$ passes through the fixed point $P$.
:::

::: {#lem-18point2}
Let $\ell$ be a line passing through $O$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be the isogonal conjugate of $\ell$. Then $N_9$ and $\infty_{\ell}$ are conjugate with respect to $\mathcal{H}$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Let $P$ be the center of $\mathcal{H}$; by @lem-14point8,
$$
\measuredangle(\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(M_{BC}),\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(N_9))=\measuredangle N_9PM_{BC}.
$$
Let $Q$ and $D$ be the reflections of $H$ across $P$ and $A_{\perp BC}$, respectively. Since both $P$ and $M_{BC}$ lie on the nine-point circle, angle chasing and homothety give
$$
\measuredangle N_9PM_{BC}=\measuredangle PA_{\perp BC}M_{AH}=\measuredangle QDA.
$$
Since $Q$ is the isogonal conjugate of $\infty_{\ell}$, if $Q'$ lies on the circumcircle with $QQ'\parallel BC$, then $AQ'\parallel\ell$.

Hence
$$
\measuredangle(\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(M_{BC}),\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(N_9))=\measuredangle QDA=\measuredangle QQ'A=\measuredangle(BC,\ell).
$$
Since $\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(M_{BC})\parallel BC$ (@lem-8point10), we have $\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(N_9)\parallel\ell$, meaning that $N_9$ and $\infty_{\ell}$ are conjugate with respect to $\mathcal{H}$.
:::

::: {#thm-18point3}
## Fonténé's Third Theorem
Let $Y$ be the isogonal conjugate of $X$. Then the nine-point circle and the pedal circle of $X$ are tangent if and only if $O,X,Y$ are collinear (equivalently, $\measuredangle XBC+\measuredangle XCA+\measuredangle XAB=90^\circ$).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Suppose the nine-point circle and the pedal circle of $X$ are tangent at $P$. By @lem-3point18, the pedal circles of $X$ and $Y$ coincide.

By @cor-14point2, $P$ is the Poncelet point of $X$ and $Y$, so the rectangular hyperbola centered at $P$ passes through $X$ and $Y$.

Thus $A,B,C,H,X,Y$ lie on a conic section; taking isogonal conjugates shows that $O,X,Y$ are collinear.

Conversely, suppose $O,X,Y$ are collinear; then by @lem-3point18, the center of the pedal circle of $X$ is $M_{XY}$.

Consider $\mathcal{H}=(ABCHXY)$; then $\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(\infty_{XY})$ passes through $M_{XY}$ (@lem-8point10) and the center $P'$ of $\mathcal{H}$.

By @lem-18point2, $\mathfrak{p}_{\mathcal{H}}(\infty_{XY})$ also passes through $N_9$, so $N_9,P',M_{XY}$ are collinear.

Since $P'$ is an intersection of the pedal circle of $X$ and the nine-point circle, and $N_9,M_{XY}$ are their respective centers, the two circles are tangent.
:::

::: {#lem-18point3}
Let $DEF$ be the intouch triangle. Then $D,E,F,M_{BC},M_{CA},M_{AB},Fe$ lie on a conic section.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
By @lem-11point2, considering the cevian triangles of $Ge$ and $G$ shows that $D,E,F,M_{BC},M_{CA},M_{AB}$ lie on a conic section $\mathcal{C}$.

Set $A_1=EF\cap M_{CA}M_{AB}$, and define $B_1$ and $C_1$ analogously.

By @lem-11point5, $DA_1,EB_1,FC_1$ concur on $\mathcal{C}$.

By @thm-18point1 applied to the pedal triangle of $I$, we see that $D,A_1,Fe$ are collinear.

Similarly, $DA_1$, $EB_1$, and $FC_1$ concur at $Fe$, so $D,E,F,M_{BC},M_{CA},M_{AB},Fe$ all lie on the conic $\mathcal{C}$.
:::

::: {#lem-18point4}
The pedal circle of $X$ is tangent to the nine-point circle if and only if the circumcevian triangle of $X$ and the pedal triangle of $X$ are homothetic.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Let $DEF$ be the pedal triangle of $X$ and $UVW$ be the circumcevian triangle of $X$.

Then $VW\parallel EF$ is equivalent to $\measuredangle(AX,VW)=\measuredangle(AX,EF)$.

We have
$$
\measuredangle(AX,VW)=\measuredangle AUV+\measuredangle UVW=\measuredangle ABX+\measuredangle XAB+\measuredangle BCX,
$$
and
$$
\measuredangle(AX,EF)=\measuredangle AXE+\measuredangle XEF=\measuredangle XAC+90^\circ+\measuredangle XAB
$$
(since $A,X,E,F$ are concyclic).

Hence the equality of the two angles is equivalent to $\measuredangle XBC+\measuredangle XCA+\measuredangle XAB=90^\circ$, which gives the result by @cor-14point4.
:::

::: {#thm-18point4}
Let $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle UVW$ be two triangles. If the perpendiculars from $P$ to $VW$, from $Q$ to $WU$, and from $R$ to $UV$ concur, then the perpendiculars from $U$ to $QR$, from $V$ to $RP$, and from $W$ to $PQ$ concur.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Fix $U,V,W,Q,R$, and let $X$ be the intersection of the perpendicular from $Q$ to $WU$ and the perpendicular from $R$ to $UV$.

Let $P$ vary along the perpendicular from $X$ to $VW$; then $P\mapsto QP\mapsto W\infty_{\perp QP}$ is projective.

Similarly, $V\infty_{\perp RP}\mapsto W\infty_{\perp QP}$ is projective. When $P=\infty_{\perp VW}$, the lines $V\infty_{\perp RP}$ and $W\infty_{\perp QP}$ coincide.

By Steiner's conic theorem, the locus of $Y=V\infty_{\perp RP}\cap W\infty_{\perp QP}$ is a line.

When $P=X$, $Y=U$; when $P=QR\cap X\infty_{\perp VW}$, $Y=\infty_{\perp QR}$.

Thus $Y$ lies on $U\infty_{\perp QR}$, so the perpendiculars from $U$ to $QR$, from $V$ to $RP$, and from $W$ to $PQ$ concur.
:::

::: {.unnumbered-env}
**Definition.**
Two triangles $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle UVW$ satisfying the condition of @thm-18point4 are called **orthologic**.
:::

::: {#lem-18point5}
The pedal circle of $X$ is tangent to the nine-point circle if and only if the circumcevian triangle of $X$ and $\triangle ABC$ are orthologic.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Suppose the pedal circle of $X$ is tangent to the nine-point circle; let $DEF$ be the pedal triangle of $X$ and $UVW$ be the circumcevian triangle of $X$.

By @lem-18point4, $VW\parallel EF$, so the perpendicular from $A$ to $VW$ is the perpendicular from $A$ to $EF$.

Angle chasing shows that the perpendicular from $A$ to $EF$ passes through the isogonal conjugate $X'$ of $X$, and similarly for $B$ and $C$, so $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle UVW$ are orthologic.

Conversely, if $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle UVW$ are orthologic, @cor-5point3 shows that $\triangle UVW\sim\triangle DEF$.

Thus the perpendicular from $B$ to $WU$ and the perpendicular from $C$ to $UV$ meet on $(BX'C)$, and similarly concur at $X'$.

Hence $\triangle UVW$ and $\triangle DEF$ are homothetic, giving the result by @lem-18point4.
:::

::: {#lem-18point6}
If the pedal circle of $X$ is tangent to the nine-point circle and $Y$ is the isogonal conjugate of $X$, then the pedal triangle of $X$ and the pedal triangle of $Y$ are orthologic.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
By @lem-18point4, the pedal triangle of $Y$ is homothetic to the circumcevian triangle of $Y$.

If $DEF$ is the pedal triangle of $X$ and $UVW$ is the circumcevian triangle of $Y$, then angle chasing gives $AY\perp EF$.

Hence $\triangle DEF$ and $\triangle UVW$ are orthologic, and by homothety the pedal triangles of $X$ and $Y$ are orthologic.
:::

::: {#lem-18point7}
There are exactly three points on the circumcircle whose Simson lines are tangent to the nine-point circle, and these three points form an equilateral triangle.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Consider $\measuredangle XBC+\measuredangle XCA+\measuredangle XAB$ from @cor-14point4.

As $X$ varies along the circumcircle, this angle changes at three times the rate of $X$, so there are three points forming an equilateral triangle for which the sum equals $90^\circ$.
:::

::: {#lem-18point8}
The orthotransversal of $X$ passes through $O$ if and only if $X$ lies on the circumcircle or the nine-point circle.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Suppose the orthotransversal $\ell$ of $X$ passes through $O$, meets the sidelines of $\triangle ABC$ at $D,E,F$, and let $PQR$ be the pedal triangle of $X$.

Then $X$ is the intersection of $(ADP)$, $(BEQ)$, and $(CFR)$, which have at most two common points.

Let $\ell$ meets $\mathcal{H}_{Je}$ again at $V$, and $VX(74)$ meets $(ABC)$ again at $X_1$.

There is an inversion centered at $H$ sending $\triangle ABC$ to $\triangle PQR$, and let this inversion map $X_1$ to $X_2$.

By @lem-17point6, $X_1$ is the intersection of the three circles, and power of a point shows that $X_2$ lies on the nine-point circle and is also the intersection of the three circles.

Hence $X$ must be $X_1$ or $X_2$, so $X$ lies on the circumcircle or the nine-point circle.

The converse follows from cross-ratio preservation in the argument above (@lem-17point6 and the map $X_2\mapsto X_1$).
:::

::: {#lem-18point9}
If $X$ lies on the nine-point circle, then the isogonal conjugate of the orthotransversal of $X$ is a rectangular hyperbola $\mathcal{H}$ whose center is $X$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Let $PQR$ be the pedal triangle of $X$, and consider the inversion centered at $H$ sending $\triangle PQR$ to $\triangle ABC$, mapping $X$ to $X_1$.

From the proof of @lem-18point8, the orthotransversal of $X_1$ coincides with that of $X$, say $\ell$; let $W$ be the isogonal conjugate of $\infty_{\ell}$.

Then the chain
$$
X\mapsto X_1\mapsto\ell\mapsto\infty_{\ell}\mapsto W\mapsto M_{HW}
$$
preserves cross ratio, and $M_{HW}$ is the center of $\mathcal{H}$ (@lem-14point3).

Substituting $X=P$ gives $\ell=AO$, so $M_{HW}=P$; similarly for $X=Q,R$.

By @thm-10point1, $X=M_{HW}$.
:::
